security_review_result.verify_chain_adversarial_trace: Traced lib/letflow/audit.ex's do_verify_chain/2 line by line: (a) recomputes chain_hash from each entry's own currently-stored columns via fields_from_entry/1 + compute_hash/1; (b) compares recomputed value against the entry's STORED chain_hash column; (c) this hash-mismatch check is the first cond branch, evaluated strictly before the prev_chain_hash linkage branch; (d) linkage is checked against prev_recomputed_hash, an accumulator holding the PREVIOUS entry's own just-recomputed (not stored) hash, threaded through the recursion. Adversarially traced the named two-entry tamper (edit entry N's content + forge entry N+1's stored prev_chain_hash to match): verify_chain/2 catches this at entry N itself (hash_mismatch) before N+1's forged linkage is ever examined -- the property holds. Confirmed further by test/letflow/audit_test.exs's real adversarial tests (lines 190-271), which tamper via raw SQL after disabling the real DB immutability trigger and assert the correct hash_mismatch vs. chain_broken distinction.
